```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4.5, fig.path="fig/")
library(CEClust)
```

# Two interfaces coexist deliberately

The new numeric solvers are selected explicitly. Historical calls remain
available because changing an old simulation's optimizer, warm starts and
repair stages without notice would make it difficult to reproduce that study.

```{r explicit}
set.seed(8)
X <- matrix(rnorm(80),ncol=2)
new <- CECfitBoundGrid(Z=X,C_grid=1,lambda_grid=c(0.8,1.2),
  optimization="em_bank",penalty="none",k0=2,B=1,
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=2,Ninit=1,max_iter=15),algo_seed=5)
new$meta[c("optimization","penalty","stability_approach","rsi_policy")]
```

## Dispatch rules

For `CECfitBoundGrid` and `CECfitLambdaGrid`, explicit `optimization`, explicit
`penalty`, a nonempty `optimizer_control`, or explicit `rsi_policy` selects
the consolidated engine. In `CECfitBoundGrid`, an explicit `grid_strategy`
or a nonempty `adaptive_control` also selects that engine. With none of these
choices, the historical linked-path engine is retained.
Changing `rsi_saturation_max` alone does not select a new engine:
state the policy and optimizer too.

For the single-fit function, `optimization="cem", penalty="none"` with an
empty control list or only a seed keeps historical CEM starts. Additional
numeric controls select the consolidated CEM search. New engines require numeric
Gaussian data; the historical unpenalized CEM supports factor and mixed inputs.

```{r historical-mixed}
mixed <- data.frame(measure=c(-2,-1.8,-1.5,1.5,1.8,2),
                    kind=factor(c("a","a","b","b","c","c")))
old <- CECclassif(mixed,C=2,lambda=1,r0=2,Nshots=1,Nloop=5,
  familyType="gaussAndDiscreteVector",optimizer_control=list(seed=6))
old$clusters
```

For a real categorical analysis, choose reference constraints and data encoding
deliberately. Converting a factor to arbitrary integer codes changes the model;
it is not a way to make the Gaussian engine handle categories.

## Defaults are not interchangeable

| Interface | Main behavior |
|:--|:--|
| Explicit `CECfitBoundGrid` solver | Independent repetitions; defaults L=B=20, thresholds 0.85/0.95/0 |
| Historical `CECfitBoundGrid` route | Linked paths and repair stages; old budgets and defaults remain |
| `CECfitLambdaGrid` | One-C diagnostics; explicit defaults L=B=10 and its own seed argument |
| Iris/breast-cancer presets | Preprocessing and budgets supplied by the preset; state thresholds and budget overrides explicitly |

In the full-grid interface the seed argument is `algo_seed`; in the one-C
interface it is `seed`. A supplied `optimizer_control$seed` takes precedence
in either route. The controls saved in the result are the reference for what
actually ran.

## Exhaustive stability is a definition change

The default now averages every original-original pair and every
original-bootstrap pair. The historical `pairwise` mode compares bootstrap
runs with one another for its bootstrap measure. `reference_bestH` compares
to a selected reference. They are not alternative names for the same average.

Old saved diagnostic values keep their original meaning. Loading an old RDS
does not recalculate them. If original/projected label vectors remain, evaluate
the new convention with `CECstability()`. A single original repetition now
gives missing algorithmic stability and RSI, rather than a spurious perfect score.

## Historical helper functions

`CECaddSmoothedDiagnostics` adds moving averages to old tables.
`CECidentifyStableLambdas` applies historical selection rules: it can use
smoothed columns, does not impose a separate algorithmic-stability threshold,
and treats its saturation bound strictly. These functions retain their meaning
for old workflows; use `CECselectStableLambdas` for the current diagram filter.

`CECextractBestPartitions` on new lambda diagnostics exposes the pooled
projected hard-score minimum. It requires `source="all"` and
`criterion="projected_H"`. Historical fixed/bootstrap/raw-score selections
are not supported on that object.

`CECrepairBestPartitionTrajectory` has nothing to improve by cross-cell
propagation on a common EM bank. It returns zero repairs there. It rejects
penalized CEM paths because the historical repair does not evaluate that penalty.
The fixed grid does not add a final best-fit CEM descent. Adaptive CEM can harmonize neighbouring cells; its `A_harm` control compares the best independent campaign partition with the final representative, separately from the exhaustive diagnostics.

## Plot filters and compact objects

Most grid views inherit the stored thresholds. The one-dimensional allocation
view in `CECplotPath(type="partitions")` still has historical threshold defaults.
Pass a `lambda_stable_obj` from `CECselectStableLambdas` explicitly to preserve
the intended filter. Static plot defaults can choose a low-REO cell for display;
they do not decide which partition should be retained scientifically.

`CECcompactGrid` removes redundant display intermediates. It keeps EM banks,
independent winner indices and original data, so rescoring remains possible.
A compact object is not an anonymized object or a set of only final labels.

## Adaptive CEM from version 0.3.0.9003

The adaptive CEM driver now separates pilot construction from independent
measurement. Versions 0.3.0.9001 and 0.3.0.9002 ran the repeated fits during
pilot construction, even where the final measurement policy excluded a cell.
The corrected driver runs one multistart pilot per new cell, with parent
starts for its children. It calibrates and refines the grid before launching
L+B independent fits only at eligible active cells. Those fits have no warm
starts. Their diagnostics remain frozen after improvements to the diagram.

Adaptive CEM now defaults to `rsi_policy="saturation_band"` with limit 0.10.
Use an explicit policy to change this. EM-bank and fixed-grid defaults remain
`"all"`. Adaptive CEM exposes the pilot, campaigns and an execution register;
`?CECresults` describes the fields. Old adaptive CEM checkpoints are a different
protocol and cannot be reused as staged campaigns.

## Scope and saved analyses

Fixed-grid behaviour is preserved. In version 0.3.0.9001,
`grid_strategy="adaptive"` also integrates four-sided extension, row-wise right
stops and refinement on both sides of partition or saturation boundaries.
Adaptive CEM adds neighbour harmonization; EM banks need none.
See `?CECadaptiveDiagram` for the controls and stopping records. No local research script
needs to be sourced to use the packaged EM or CEM engines.

Keep the package version, the preprocessing code and `sessionInfo()` with
the RDS. For paired scoring of one EM bank, save each result under a distinct
filename. Neither the library version nor a filename alone documents which
optimizer, penalty and diagnostic convention a study used; the result metadata
records those choices.
